title: Pull Out Pantry Organization Ideas: Baskets, Drawers and Racks That Fit
seoTitle: Pull Out Pantry Organization Ideas That Fit
excerpt: Pull out pantry organization ideas for deep base cabinets, narrow gaps and existing shelves: how to measure, what to store in each pull-out and how to keep it organized.
imageCaption: A tall pull-out pantry cabinet extended beside the refrigerator, with jars of pasta, rice and grains on sliding shelves. AI-generated illustration of a general idea.
content: The best **pull out pantry organization ideas** bring the back of the cabinet to you. Install sliding wire baskets in deep base cabinets, use a narrow pull-out rack in the gap beside the fridge or stove, add slide-out drawers to existing pantry shelves, and group food by how often you reach for it so the front of every drawer holds the things you use daily. Measure first, keep heavy items low, and label the front edge of each basket so everyone in the house puts things back in the same place.

A pull-out pantry works because it changes how you reach. In a fixed cabinet you lean in, move three jars and still cannot see what is in the back corner. On a slide, the whole shelf comes out into the light and you look down at it from above. That is why pull-outs suit deep base cabinets, tall narrow spaces and pantries where food keeps getting lost behind newer groceries. This guide covers the main types, how to measure, what to store where and the mistakes that make a pull-out pantry feel crowded again after a month.
## Pull Out Pantry Organization Ideas at a Glance
Each idea solves a different kind of space. Most kitchens combine two or three of them rather than replacing every shelf.

| Idea | Best space | What it holds well | Install |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pull-out wire basket in a base cabinet | Deep lower cabinets | Canned goods, jars, bottles, pots | Screws into the cabinet floor |
| Narrow pull-out spice rack | Slim cabinets and gaps | Spices, oils, sauces | Slides fitted inside the cabinet |
| Slide-out drawer on an existing shelf | Walk-in or reach-in pantry shelves | Snacks, packets, baking supplies | Adhesive or screw mount, depending on the model |
| Two-tier pull-out | Cabinets with spare height | Cans on the bottom, small jars on top | Screws into the cabinet floor |
| Tall pull-out pantry cabinet | Gap beside the fridge | Dry goods for the whole week | Cabinet installation, often a pro job |
| Clear bins on pull-out shelves | Any pull-out | Loose packets and small items | No tools |
| Over-the-door rack as a partner | Pantry door | Spices, small jars, wraps | Hooks over the door or wall mount |
Start with the cabinet that frustrates you most. For most people that is the deep corner or the cabinet under the counter where canned food disappears.
## Measure the Cabinet Before You Buy Anything

Pull-out organizers fail for one reason more than any other: they do not fit. A basket that is half an inch too wide will not clear the hinges, and one that is too deep will stop the door from closing. Take three measurements of the inside of the cabinet and write them down before you shop.

![Diagram of three cabinet measurements for a pull-out organizer: A is the inside width at the narrowest point, B is the height from the cabinet floor to the lowest obstruction, and C is the depth from the door to the back wall, with notes on measuring between hinges and comparing against the minimum opening. Diagram: Sesoris](/images/blog/pull-out-pantry-organization-ideas-measure.webp)

**Width** is the most important number. Measure at the narrowest point of the opening, which is usually between the hinges or the lip of a face frame, not wall to wall inside the box. **Height** runs from the cabinet floor to the lowest thing in the way, such as a fixed shelf, a drawer box above or a pipe under the sink. **Depth** runs from the inside of the door or frame to the back wall.

Every organizer lists a minimum opening. Compare all three of your numbers with it, and check what sticks into the cabinet from the sides, like hinge plates or a center stile on double doors. If your cabinet has a face frame, measure the frame opening as well as the box behind it, because the frame is often the narrower of the two.
## Pull-Out Wire Baskets for Deep Base Cabinets

A sliding wire basket is the workhorse of pull-out pantry organization. It sits on two rails screwed to the cabinet floor and turns a dark, deep cabinet into a shelf that comes out to meet you. Wire lets you see the contents from above and lets crumbs fall through to a removable liner instead of collecting in corners.

![A chrome wire pull-out cabinet organizer on its slide rails with a white liner, holding three round plates standing on edge, shown from the side against a white background. Photo: Sesoris product catalog](/images/blog/pull-out-pantry-organization-ideas-wire-basket.webp)

Our [14 in. pull-out cabinet organizer](/product/pull-out-cabinet-organizer-14-inch) is a good example of what to check. The basket is 14 in. wide, 21 in. deep and 2.5 in. tall, it needs an opening of at least 15.1 in. wide, 21 in. deep and 3.3 in. tall, and it is rated for 28.6 lbs (13 kg). Wider cabinets can take the [20 in. version](/product/pull-out-cabinet-organizer-20-inch), which extends to 41.8 in. on ball-bearing rails and needs an opening of at least 22.3 in. wide, 22.2 in. deep and 7.3 in. tall.

Load the basket with weight in mind. Canned goods and glass jars are heavy, so spread them across the basket rather than stacking them at the front edge. Keep the heaviest items in the lowest cabinet and lighter boxes higher up. If you have more than one basket in the same cabinet, leave enough height between them to lift a jar out without tilting it.
## Narrow Pull-Outs for Spices, Oils and Sauces

The slim cabinet next to the stove is often wasted on baking sheets that fall over. A narrow two-tier pull-out turns that sliver of space into the most useful cabinet in the kitchen. Spice jars stand in a single row you can read at a glance, and oil bottles stay upright on the lower tier.

![A narrow two-tier chrome pull-out spice rack with white shelf liners on its slide rails, shown empty on a white background. Photo: Sesoris product catalog](/images/blog/pull-out-pantry-organization-ideas-spice-rack.webp)

Our [2-tier pull-out spice rack](/product/pull-out-spice-rack-2-tier-4-inch) is 4.33 in. wide, 8.46 in. deep and 10.43 in. tall, fits openings at least 5.51 in. wide and 11.61 in. deep, and is rated at 22 lbs (10 kg) per tier. That size suits a filler cabinet or the space beside a range. Put the spices you use every week at the front of the top tier and the rarely used ones at the back.

If you do not have a slim cabinet, the same idea works on a wall or door. Our guides to [microwave wall shelf ideas](/blog/microwave-wall-shelf-ideas) and [pantry storage racks](/blog/pantry-storage-rack) show how to pair a pull-out with vertical storage nearby.
## Slide-Out Drawers for Existing Pantry Shelves

You do not need to rebuild a walk-in pantry to get pull-out storage. Slide-out drawers sit on top of the shelves you already have and give the deepest shelves a front edge you can pull toward you. They are especially useful on lower shelves, where you would otherwise crouch and dig.

![A wide chrome pull-out cabinet organizer fully extended on its slide rails, an empty wire basket with a frosted liner, shown on a white background. Photo: Sesoris product catalog](/images/blog/pull-out-pantry-organization-ideas-wide-basket.webp)

Our [slide-out cabinet drawer](/product/slide-out-cabinet-drawer-black) is made of black carbon steel, measures 11.81 x 16.92 x 3.15 in., slides out up to 13 in. and holds up to 55 lbs (25 kg). It mounts with adhesive tapes, so it suits renters who cannot drill into shelves. Check the product instructions and the surface of your shelf before you rely on adhesive mounting for heavy loads.

For deep shelves that are too wide for a single drawer, combine a slide-out drawer on one side with clear bins on the other. Our [deep pantry organization ideas](/blog/deep-pantry-organization-ideas) and [wire shelf pantry organization ideas](/blog/wire-shelf-pantry-organization-ideas) go further into layouts for walk-in and wire-shelved pantries.
## What to Store in Each Pull-Out

A pull-out pantry stays organized when every drawer has a job. Group food by type and by how often you reach for it, then give each group its own drawer or basket. The table below is a starting point you can adjust to how your household cooks.

| Pull-out | Store here | Keep at the front |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lowest base basket | Canned goods, jars, heavy bottles | Cans you use every week |
| Upper base basket | Pasta, rice, grains in containers | Open packages |
| Narrow two-tier rack | Spices, oils, vinegars, sauces | Salt, pepper and cooking oil |
| Slide-out drawer on a pantry shelf | Snacks and breakfast items | Kids' snacks at their height |
| Clear bin inside a basket | Packets, sauces, seasoning mixes | The packet you will use next |

Decant dry goods like rice, pasta and cereal into clear containers with tight lids so they stack and stay fresh. Our comparison of [glass, plastic and stainless steel food storage containers](/blog/glass-vs-plastic-vs-stainless-steel-food-storage-containers) and our [airtight food storage containers guide](/blog/air-tight-food-storage-containers-guide-2026) help you choose. Square containers waste less space in a basket than round ones.
## Keep Food Rotating: First In, First Out

Pull-outs make it easy to see everything, which also makes it easy to rotate food. When you unpack groceries, put the new items at the back of the drawer and slide the older ones to the front. That simple habit means you use food before it expires instead of finding a forgotten can two years later.

Check expiration dates once a month when you write the shopping list. A pull-out basket takes seconds to scan from above. Anything close to its date moves to the front, and anything you will not use goes to a food bank while it is still good. For a full reset of a crowded pantry, follow our [step-by-step pantry organization tutorial](/blog/how-to-organize-your-pantry-step-by-step-tutorial-2026).
## Label the Front Edge and Keep It Simple

Labels tell everyone in the house where things go back. On a pull-out, the best place for a label is the front edge of the basket or drawer, where you can read it before you open the cabinet door fully. Use short category names like "Cans", "Pasta and Rice" or "Baking" rather than listing every item.

Resist the urge to buy one of every organizer. A basket packed with small bins becomes hard to pull and harder to clean. Start with the baskets, live with them for two weeks, then add a bin only where small items keep tipping over. Our [pantry organization bins guide](/blog/pantry-organization-bins) explains which bin shapes work inside baskets.
## A Weekend Plan for a Pull-Out Pantry

1. **Empty the cabinets you want to change.** Put everything on the counter so you can see how much you really store.
2. **Toss expired food and group the rest.** Make piles for cans, dry goods, spices, snacks and baking.
3. **Measure each cabinet.** Record width at the narrowest point, height to the lowest obstruction and depth.
4. **Choose organizers that fit.** Compare your numbers with each product's minimum opening and weight rating.
5. **Install the rails and baskets.** Follow the instructions, check that each basket slides fully and the door closes.
6. **Load by weight and frequency.** Heavy and everyday items low and in front, rarely used items higher or behind.
7. **Label the front edges.** Short category names so everyone puts things back.

If you are planning a bigger pantry update, our guides to [pantry cabinet ideas](/blog/pantry-cabinet-ideas), [small pantry ideas](/blog/small-pantry-ideas) and [pantry shelving ideas](/blog/pantry-shelving-ideas) show how pull-outs fit into a full pantry plan.
## Common Mistakes With Pull-Out Pantries

- **Measuring wall to wall instead of the opening.** Hinges and face frames make the usable width smaller.
- **Ignoring the weight rating.** A basket loaded past its rating can sag or stop sliding smoothly.
- **Stacking heavy jars at the front edge.** Spread weight across the basket so it pulls evenly.
- **Filling every gap with tiny bins.** Too many containers make the drawer heavy and hard to clean.
- **Forgetting the door swing.** A basket that hits the door or hinge when it slides out needs a narrower model.
- **Skipping rotation.** Without first in, first out, the back of a pull-out becomes the new forgotten corner.
## Frequently Asked Questions
**Q: What is a pull-out pantry?**

A pull-out pantry uses shelves, baskets or drawers on slide rails so the contents come out of the cabinet toward you. It can be a tall cabinet with sliding shelves or pull-out baskets added to ordinary base cabinets and pantry shelves.
**Q: How do I measure for a pull-out pantry organizer?**

Measure the inside width at the narrowest point of the opening, usually between hinges or a face frame, the height from the cabinet floor to the lowest obstruction, and the depth from the door to the back wall. Compare all three with the organizer's minimum opening.
**Q: Can I add pull-out shelves to existing cabinets?**

Yes. Many pull-out baskets screw to the floor of an existing base cabinet, and slide-out drawers can sit on top of existing pantry shelves. Check the minimum opening, the weight rating and whether hinges or a center stile block the slide.
**Q: How much weight can a pull-out basket hold?**

It depends on the model, so check the rating before loading it. For example, our 14 in. and 20 in. pull-out cabinet organizers are rated for 28.6 lbs (13 kg), and our slide-out cabinet drawer is rated for 55 lbs (25 kg).
**Q: Are there pull-out pantry options for renters?**

Some slide-out drawers mount with adhesive tapes instead of screws, which suits rentals. For screw-mounted baskets, ask your landlord first, and keep the original shelves so you can restore the cabinet when you move out.
**Q: What should go in a narrow pull-out cabinet?**

Narrow pull-outs work best for spices, oils, vinegars and sauces, because bottles and jars stand in a single row you can read from above. Keep everyday items like salt, pepper and cooking oil at the front.
**Q: How do I keep a pull-out pantry organized?**
Give each pull-out a single category, label the front edge, put new groceries behind older ones, and scan the drawers once a month for food close to its date.
**Q: Should I use wire baskets or solid drawers?**

Wire baskets let you see contents from above and let crumbs fall to a removable liner, which makes them good for cans and jars. Solid drawers suit small packets and snacks that could slip through wire.
## Final Thoughts

Pull out pantry organization ideas all aim at the same thing: no more digging. Measure each cabinet carefully, choose baskets and drawers that fit the opening and the weight you store, and give every pull-out one job with a clear label on the front edge. Rotate food from back to front as you shop, and the pantry stays easy to use long after the weekend you set it up.
